note: Forest Service campground on the south-east shore of 22-acre, spring-fed Logger's Lake (electric motors only), in Shannon County south-west of Bunker; small swim beach, boat ramps and a fishing pier. Reached by 6 miles of Dent County Road 565 and 1 mile of FR 2193: the Forest Service says 4WD is not required but the last part of the road is rough and a high-clearance vehicle is highly recommended. Sites must be booked at least 5 days ahead; April and October nights are first come, first served. --Claude
summary: Confirmed; fees $15 (rec.gov) kept with the FS page's stale $10 noted; added no-hookup water/sewer false, 14 paved back-in sites (FS 30-ft max), vault toilets + water, season 04-09..11-01 (2026), rec.gov booking May-Sep, 180 days. Access road: high clearance 'highly recommended', 4WD 'not required' - kept with a caveat. Pin moves 1.2 km; waterfront ask lakeview -> lakefront; phone to add.
flags: ACCESS ROAD (keep with caveat): Forest Service, https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/marktwain/recreation/loggers-lake-recreation-area, 'Directions': 'A 4WD vehicle is not required, but the last part of the road to Logger's Lake is rough in terrain, high clearance vehicle is highly recommended.' The same page's General Information says 'Vehicle Clearance: No restrictions'. Recreation.gov notice: 'Road leading into campground is gravel with rough patches. Speed should be kept to a minimum over rough road surfaces.' No 4WD requirement or recommendation and nothing saying cars or RVs should not attempt it, so kept and caveated in the note. Context: the operator of Little Sinkin Creek RV Resort (14568, ~5 km north) warns that the GPS route via 'CR 565 / Lincoln Ave / Logger's Lake Rd' is 'not RV friendly' - the same road the FS directions use.

PIN MOVE: stored 37.3800,-91.2700 is in woods ~1.2 km south-west of the campground. Recreation.gov site points (005-014) and the FS page's 37.387666,-91.260922 put the loop at the east shore; move to 37.3878,-91.2607 (loop centre).

WATERFRONT ASK lakeview -> lakefront: FS 'The campground area is located on the southeast lakeshore and all sites have a view of the lake, with only light vegetation in between'; recreation.gov tags all 10 sites 'Proximity to Water: Lakefront'. Imagery: sites 008/010/011 sit on the west side of the loop on an open grass peninsula, the loop road behind them (east), no day use between (the day-use area is to the right of the campground); the image was taken at a low pool, but the old shoreline edge is ~30-40 m from sites 010/011. Site photos 010 and 011 (2019) show table, mown grass, then open water close beyond. Earns the 50 m open-apron rule for some sites in my reading; AWH to decide (waterfront is a flag).

FEES CONFLICT: recreation.gov $15 single (2026 Peak 04-09..10-26; 2027 and 2028 at $15 too) vs FS page 'Single Site: $10 per night, Double Site: $20 per night'. Kept $15 (what rec.gov sells; trust rec.gov over agency pages).

SITES: FS says 14 single non-electric sites; recreation.gov's catalog has 10 (005-014; 001-004 not listed). FS 'Maximum recommended size is 30 feet' vs rec.gov 'Max Vehicle Length 40' - wrote the FS 30 ft (a 23-ft rig fits either way).

BOOKING: FS 'Reservation needed for camping sites', 6 months ahead, at least 5 days ahead (rec.gov reservationCutOff 4). 2027 is reservable 05-01..09-30 and first come, first served 04-10..04-30 and 10-01..10-30 (rec.gov 'Not Reservable' in April 2027). Season: FS 'Open April 9 - November 1, 2026' replaces the approximate Apr-Oct (derived, not manual).
